data.title: Alfa Laval Sets 2030 Sales Target Of SEK 100 Bln; Sees SEK 8 Bln Capex For 2027-2028
data.description:
STOCKHOLM (dpa-AFX) - Alfa Laval AB (ALFA.ST), a Swedish industrial engineering company, outlined its long-term financial targets and investment plans at its Capital Markets Day, targeting sales of SEK 100 billion by 2030.

The company plans capital expenditure of SEK 8 billion during 2027-2028, including SEK 4 billion for Energy, SEK 1.2 billion for Food & Pharma and SEK 3 billion for Ocean. A further SEK 6 billion is expected to be spent during 2029-2030.

Alfa Laval's financial targets over a business cycle include, Sales growth of 7%, Adjusted EBITA margin of 17%, and Return on capital employed (ROCE) of 20%. These compare with its last three-year average annual sales growth of 11.9%, adjusted EBITA margin of 16.7% and ROCE of 22.8%.

In Stockholm, Alfa Laval shares closed down 1.45% at SEK 528.40 on Wednesday.

data.title: Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

Novartis raised its peak sales estimates for key drugs Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio, saying this reinforces confidence in the company's midterm outlook.

The company said it now has nine in-market products with potential to generate annual peak sales of between $3 billion and $10 billion, as well as 10 in late-stage development that could bring in multibillion-dollar sales at their peak.

Novartis also said it is on track to return to a core operating profit margin above 40% by 2029, as previously indicated.

data.title: Asian stocks fail to get a lift from Anthropic's IPO pricing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic's blockbuster IPO pricing fails to lift Asian stocks
  • US stock futures gain in anticipation of the biggest-ever IPO
  • Investor worries over AI trade cast shadow
  • Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to 19-month high

By Ankur Banerjee

Asian stocks slid on Thursday as fears over the AI trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials left sentiment fragile ahead of a blockbuster market debut from Anthropic after the Claude chatbot maker scored the biggest IPO ever.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about $1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing.

"I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI," he said. "I think much of that boils down to future investment growth."

Traders' immediate reaction was to push US stock futures higher, with Nasdaq futures up 1.3% and S&P futures 0.36% higher. European stock futures rose 0.3%.

However, Asian equities slumped, led by Taiwanese stocks, with the Taipei benchmark index TWSE:TAIEX sliding 4.4%. South Korea's KOSPI and Nikkei inched higher in choppy trading.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell 1.7% to a seven-month low. The index was set for a decline of nearly 6% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since early March.

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken over the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build related infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, said the Anthropic IPO is a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won’t settle the debate," she said. "There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it’ll take a few things to climb it."

Investors are also focusing on an unprecedented three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

DOLLAR FIRMS ON HAWKISH FED

In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of a rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0964, hovering near its lowest since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 159.48 per US dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against six other currencies, was 0.1% higher at 103.92, a 19-month high.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

The comments followed hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, causing markets to brace for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD."

The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low after soft jobs data cemented the view that Australian rates have likely peaked. The Aussie last bought $0.6686, down 0.4%. [AUD/]

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were at $92.11 a barrel, set for a third weekly decline.

data.title: South Korean Tourism Stocks Rally on Hopes for Expanded China Trade Pact
data.description:
By Kwanwoo Jun

South Korean tourism stocks rallied Thursday on hopes that an expanded free-trade agreement between Seoul and Beijing would boost Chinese visitor arrivals.

China and South Korea earlier this week reached a deal to broaden the scope of their 2015 FTA to include sectors such as tourism, entertainment and investment services, wrapping up years of negotiations, according to President Lee Jae Myung's office in Seoul.

The deal, announced Wednesday after a bilateral summit between Lee and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, allows South Korean travel agencies to organize outbound travel from 23 regions in China, according to South Korea's trade ministry.

In Seoul trading Thursday, travel company Hanatour Service jumped as much as 28%, while budget airline Jeju Air climbed up to 25%. Hotel Shilla, which operates hotels and duty-free shops, rose as much as 13%.

"The expansion of channels to attract Chinese tourists to South Korea is expected to further boost passenger demand on China routes," Hanwha Investment & Securities analyst Park Su-young said after the deal was reached.

The aviation, entertainment and leisure industries stand to gain from the latest Korea-China pact, with aviation likely to be the biggest beneficiary, she wrote in a research note.

Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn viewed Jeju Air as a key beneficiary of the expanded FTA, citing the company's greater exposure to the Chinese market than any other South Korean low-cost carrier.

Routes to mainland China account for 8% of the South Korean budget airline's revenue, and that share could increase further, Ahn said.

In a statement on Wednesday's expanded deal, President Lee's office said South Korea and China should continue immigration measures to facilitate travel between the two countries to help boost bilateral people-to-people exchanges.

The office expects the number of people traveling between the two countries to reach 10 million this year and hopes it will eventually return to the 13 million recorded in 2016.

Exchanges have been constrained since Beijing allegedly restricted Chinese group tours to South Korea following Seoul's decision in 2016 to deploy a U.S. missile-defense system despite Chinese protests. Beijing has denied imposing a ban.

data.title: Senores Pharmaceuticals Secures PIC/S GMP Certification For Gujarat Facility
data.description:
The certification from Ukraine’s medicines regulator is expected to expand the company’s regulatory pathway into semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets

Senores Pharmaceuticals Limited has secured Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) certification for the manufacturing facility of its subsidiary, Ratnatris Pharmaceuticals Private Limited, in Mehsana, Gujarat, on 17 November, 2026, strengthening its regulatory pathway to enter semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets.

The certification was issued by Ukraine’s State Service on Medicines and Drugs Control (SMDC), with the certificate of GMP compliance dated 16 November, 2026, and received by the company on 17 November. The approval covers the facility’s injectable and oral solid dosage manufacturing operations, enabling Senores Pharmaceuticals to expand the reach of its product portfolio and pursue regulatory opportunities across additional markets.

Expanding Market Access

Commenting on the development, Swapnil Shah, Managing Director of Senores Pharmaceuticals, said the certification would open strategic markets that the company had not been able to serve previously. “The PIC/S approval will open many strategic markets that we couldn't serve so far. With approval of both, injectable and oral solids, our diverse and strategic portfolio’s reach will be further enhanced, and will continue to give long term growth and sustained profitability,” Shah said.

PIC/S GMP certification establishes compliance with internationally recognised pharmaceutical manufacturing quality standards and can support companies in pursuing regulatory approvals in markets that rely on recognised GMP inspection frameworks.

The certification is expected to strengthen Senores Pharmaceuticals’ international expansion strategy by providing additional regulatory access for its manufacturing capabilities across injectable and oral solid formulations. With the Mehsana facility receiving the certification, the company aims to broaden its market reach and leverage its manufacturing portfolio to pursue growth opportunities in semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets.

data.title: Ransomware Attacks Jump 20%; Experts Warn Businesses Face A New Threat Baseline
data.description:
Ransomware, data theft and AI-enabled attacks are escalating, while experts warn that cybersecurity investments are failing to keep pace with the evolving threat landscape

A series of cyber incidents targeting organisations across industries in recent weeks has highlighted an intensifying threat landscape, with attacks affecting technology, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, financial services and public infrastructure. From ransomware and data theft to supply-chain compromises, the incidents have exposed how vulnerabilities in third-party services can affect multiple organisations.

The latest incident this week involving digital experience platform Optimizely brought this risk into focus after malicious JavaScript was injected into websites belonging to 178 organisations, including BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, HSBC and IKEA. Discovered on 16 November, the attack exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation account sign-up process, allowing an unauthorised party to add malicious code to customer projects.

The scripts were designed to steal payment card information, capture browser cookies and screenshots, and replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Optimizely said it had fixed the vulnerability and removed the malicious code. The incident did not establish that the internal networks of all 178 organisations had been breached; the code was delivered through the shared third-party platform.

Steve Vintz, Co-CEO of Tenable, noted that the incident showed how organisations' exposure extended beyond their own networks. "The attack surface no longer ends at the edge of your network. It extends to every external asset and connection you depend on, whoever owns it," he said, adding that exposure management needed to cover assets organisations did not directly own.

Third-party Vulnerabilities Under Scrutiny

The Optimizely incident follows several other cyberattacks and data breaches reported during October and November.In the energy sector, Norwegian oil and gas major Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on some IT systems on 17 November, while saying its production operations remained unaffected.

In France, attacks on refrigeration control systems affected around 700 supermarket locations, including outlets linked to Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour and Intermarché. Japan's retailer Nitori Holdings reported unauthorised access that could have exposed information relating to as many as 37.62 million records.

Taiwanese semiconductor manufacturer TSMC also confirmed a breach involving an unnamed cloud service provider that exposed employee information, but said its own systems and customer data were not compromised.

Other incidents included a breach involving a third-party email distribution service used by the Osaka city government, exposing more than one million email addresses, and a suspected ransomware attack on Osaka Metropolitan University that disrupted internal systems.

Separately, ransomware attacks exploiting vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers affected organisations across sectors, including water utilities, telecommunications, regional government and education.

The Numbers Behind The Cyber Surge

While the incidents have received considerable attention, cybersecurity experts said the increase is not merely a consequence of greater media coverage. Threat intelligence data points to a rise in actual cybercrime activity, particularly ransomware.

Mandar Patil, EVP at Cyble, said the company's research arm, Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs (CRIL), recorded 3,836 ransomware attacks globally in the first half of 2026, compared with 3,201 in the same period last year, an increase of around 20 per cent.

The pace accelerated in the following months. August was the most active month of 2026, with 1,034 organisations publicly named as victims by 88 ransomware groups. Attack volumes rose 60 per cent in July and another 25 per cent in August, reversing a three-month decline between March and June.

Patil said the increase was becoming a sustained trend rather than a temporary spike. “We do not read this as a seasonal spike. CRIL treats it as a new baseline, which means security planning based on first-half 2026 volumes is now running about 41 per cent below actual activity.”

"The surge is driven by scale rather than new technology. CRIL attributes it to affiliate recruitment and the exploitation of internet-facing infrastructure, not to new encryption capability, and gangs are using AI to speed up intrusions," Patil added.

Subhajeet Singha, Senior TRU Researcher at Acronis Threat Research Unit, said multiple independent datasets pointed to a rise in cyber incidents, with the scale of exposure increasing alongside the number of breaches.

"Clusit recorded 4,911 serious incidents globally in the first half of 2026, a 71 per cent jump from the same period last year," Singha said. In the US, the Identity Theft Resource Center (ITRC) tracked 1,803 data compromises during the same period, compared with 1,732 a year earlier. However, the number of victim notices crossed 471 million in six months, already exceeding the total recorded for all of 2025.

Singha said the growing use of AI was lowering the barriers to cybercrime, allowing individuals to carry out attacks at a scale that previously required greater resources. "In recent attacks, multiple AI agents have been used by just one individual to make large scale attacks. This makes it easier (in terms of skill and cost) to conduct attacks meaning there are more attackers, and therefore more targets," he added.

Singha also flagged third-party and supply-chain vulnerabilities as major contributors to the rise, as a breach involving a trusted service provider can expose several organisations that depend on its systems.

Why Critical Sectors Are In The Crosshairs

Manufacturing, professional services, IT and IT-enabled services, healthcare and financial services are among the sectors experiencing heightened cyber activity. According to CRIL, manufacturing recorded 151 ransomware victims in August, followed by professional services with 147, IT and IT-enabled services with 126, and healthcare with 98. BFSI was the most affected sector in terms of data breaches during the first half of 2026.

The nature of attacks is also changing, with cybercriminals relying on data theft and extortion rather than encrypting victims' systems. In one CL0P campaign exploiting CVE-2026-12569, more than 40 organisations were reportedly compromised through data theft without file encryption.

Singha said financial services, healthcare, government, manufacturing and critical infrastructure remained attractive targets because of the sensitive information they hold and the disruption that prolonged downtime can cause. He also highlighted the growing use of identity-based attacks, credential theft, supply-chain breaches and the exploitation of unpatched software vulnerabilities.

India Sees Rising Cyber Threats

India is facing a sharp increase in ransomware activity. According to CRIL, the country recorded 45 ransomware incidents in the first quarter of 2026, making it the most targeted country in the Asia-Pacific region. This was a 165 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year. In August, India recorded 24 claimed ransomware victims, accounting for around one-sixth of Asia-Pacific claims and ranking seventh globally.

Patil identified The Gentlemen, Sinobi, Vect, Tengu and CL0P among the groups actively targeting Indian organisations. He also flagged repeat attacks, with organisations often being targeted again after their initial breach became public.

Hacktivist groups focused on the Indian subcontinent have also carried out website defacements, distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and information operations against government, telecom, media and commercial organisations.

Nitin Jhunjhunwala, Partner at Deloitte India, said India was experiencing similar pressures to global markets, particularly across education, healthcare and manufacturing. "Cyber risk is unquestionably intensifying. We are seeing not only more attacks, but attacks that are faster, cheaper to execute and increasingly AI-enabled," he added.

Jhunjhunwala said AI-driven attacks had risen 56 per cent year-on-year, while education, healthcare and manufacturing accounted for nearly 47 per cent of detected threats in recent Indian telemetry.

Cybersecurity Spending Struggles To Keep Pace

The growing threat landscape is prompting organisations to increase cybersecurity investments, with priorities shifting towards identity security, automation, vulnerability management and faster incident detection.

Jhunjhunwala said financial services, insurance and consumer-facing businesses were increasing investments in these areas. The response was moving away from traditional perimeter security towards "identity, AI-enabled defence, rapid detection and cyber resilience".

Singha said banking and financial services, healthcare, telecommunications and large enterprises were leading the increase in spending, driven by regulatory requirements and the potential cost of security failures. Organisations were prioritising recovery and resilience, identity and access security, round-the-clock monitoring and protection against AI-related risks.

Patil, however, cautioned that higher investments did not necessarily mean organisations were adequately prepared for current threat levels. "Investment is rising, but our data shows many organizations are still budgeting for a threat level that has already passed," he added, arguing that security planning based on first-half ransomware volumes was running about 41 per cent below actual activity.

He recommended risk-based patching of internet-facing systems, phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for third parties, network segmentation, offline backup testing and monitoring dark web leak sites and access markets.

Indian organisations face growing pressure to strengthen their cyber defences, with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, setting out a framework for data protection and breach-related obligations.

The DPDP regime is being implemented in phases, with most substantive compliance requirements scheduled to take effect from May 2027. CERT-In directions and sector-specific regulations also add to the compliance requirements.

However, the response remains uneven. While larger companies are strengthening their security strategies, limited budgets and a shortage of skilled personnel continue to leave mid-sized businesses and SMEs exposed. Ensuring that regulatory compliance translates into stronger security measures and faster recovery from attacks remains a key challenge.

Aditi Das

data.title: RWE's Americas CEO Andrew Flanagan to Depart
data.description:
By Aimee Look

RWE said its Americas Chief Executive Officer Andrew Flanagan will leave the company for a new opportunity at the end of the year, and that the search for a replacement is underway.

The German renewable energy company said that Ingmar Ritzenhofen, who is currently chief commercial officer and a board member of RWE Americas and RWE Supply & Trading, will serve as interim CEO for the region.

Flanagan has helped RWE bolster its role in the Americas over the past few years, said Markus Krebber, CEO of RWE.

At the same time, Tim Nelson and Corey Hopper will join RWE Americas' board immediately, the company said.

Write to Aimee Look at aimee.look@wsj.com
